english_draft: This is a retrospective reconstruction of a preview of Micron Technology's fiscal Q2 2026 earnings report, which was scheduled for March 18, 2026. The reconstruction uses only information from the official earnings release for fiscal Q1 2026, published on December 17, 2025. It is not a contemporaneous forecast. In fiscal Q1 2026, ended November 27, 2025, Micron reported record revenue of $13.64 billion, up from $11.32 billion in the prior quarter and $8.71 billion in the year-ago quarter. GAAP diluted EPS was $4.60; non-GAAP diluted EPS was $4.78. GAAP gross margin reached 56.0% of revenue; non-GAAP gross margin reached 56.8%. Operating cash flow was $8.41 billion. Adjusted free cash flow was $3.9 billion, versus $803 million last quarter. Management said AI demand acceleration and Micron execution drove the record quarter and highest ever free cash flow. For fiscal Q2 2026, Micron guided revenue of $18.70 billion, plus or minus $400 million. Non-GAAP gross margin guidance was 68.0%, plus or minus 1.0 percentage point. Non-GAAP EPS guidance was $8.42, plus or minus $0.20. GAAP EPS guidance was $8.19, plus or minus $0.20. All four business units improved gross and operating margin year over year and sequentially. Cloud Memory revenue was $5.28 billion with a 66% gross margin. Core Data Center revenue was $2.38 billion with a 51% gross margin. Mobile and Client revenue was $4.26 billion with a 54% gross margin. Automotive and Embedded revenue was $1.72 billion with a 45% gross margin. The balance sheet showed cash and marketable investments of $12.0 billion. The company declared a quarterly dividend of $0.115 per share. The key questions for the fiscal Q2 report were whether the AI-related data center strength would continue, whether HBM supply constraints or pricing remained favorable, and whether the rest of the business, including mobile and client, would continue to recover. The main upside risk was that AI demand and pricing could exceed guidance. The main downside risk was that capacity constraints, cost inflation, or weaker traditional markets could slow the rapid margin expansion. The verification points in the March 18 report were revenue, gross margin, EPS, free cash flow, and business unit margins versus the December 17 guidance.
